headline: Town and school officials opened FY28 budget reviews warning of override needs, while advancing zoning changes to expand over-55 housing.
synopsis: Southborough town departments and regional schools presented preliminary FY28 budgets showing severe service and staffing cuts under level-funded scenarios, prompting early preparations for a potential May operational override vote. The Select Board and Zoning Board of Appeals reviewed zoning proposals to remove the municipal cap on 55-plus housing developments while mandating 12.5 percent affordable units. The Planning Board conducted a technical review of lighting and stormwater for the proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco, continuing the hearing into December. In addition, the Capital Improvement and Planning Committee confronted a $1 million funding gap between departmental capital requests and municipal revenue placeholders, while the Community Preservation Committee announced a $632,000 state grant for the Harold E. Fay Memorial Park renovation.

highlights.title: Select Board begins FY28 budget review and override preparations
highlights.why: Department heads presented level-service and level-funded budget scenarios to the Select Board, warning that level funding would force the loss of a police officer, reductions to fire shift minimums, and the elimination of 15 school staff positions.

highlights.title: Town advances zoning amendment to lift cap on senior housing
highlights.why: The Select Board voted to sponsor a Town Meeting warrant article that removes the 7 percent cap on 55-plus developments and requires at least 12.5 percent of units to be affordable.

highlights.title: Regional School Committee reviews preliminary $32.4 million budget
highlights.why: The regional high school district presented a preliminary 3.01 percent budget increase and approved a health insurance agreement saving $450,000, while preparing a 0 percent scenario that would eliminate five positions.

highlights.title: Capital requests exceed town placeholder by $1 million
highlights.why: Town departments submitted $2.2 million in FY28 capital requests against a $1.2 million non-debt placeholder, prompting the committee to consider adjusting town bonding thresholds.

highlights.title: Costco wholesale site plan and lighting review
highlights.why: The Planning Board evaluated dark-sky exterior lighting fixtures, landscaping species, and stormwater containment ponds for the proposed store at 21 Coslin Drive before continuing the hearing to December 14.

highlights.title: State awards $632,000 grant for Fay Memorial Park
highlights.why: Southborough received an award of up to $632,000 from the Land and Water Conservation Fund to cover roughly half of the estimated $1.4 million park renovation project.

Committee meeting to rank and vote on FY28 capital project recommendations
